topStories.headline: Downtown SF Hits Record Visitor Numbers as Q2 Report Shows Tourism Surge
topStories.dek: The Downtown SF Partnership's Q2 2026 market report shows record non-resident visits topping 10.54 million, surging hotel revenue, and falling office vacancy across all building classes.
topStories.body:
Downtown San Francisco's recovery is registering in hard numbers. The Downtown San Francisco Partnership's Q2 2026 Market Report — released this month — shows record non-resident visits of 10.54 million for the quarter, alongside a hotel Revenue Per Available Room (RevPAR) increase of 15.8% and falling office vacancy across all building classes in the district. Average daily visits to the district are up 34.7% over Q4 2025, with Partnership data noting that major events and ground-floor business openings are fueling the surge.

The broader visitor economy is also brightening. The San Francisco Travel Association projected in May that the city will welcome 24.2 million visitors in 2026, with visitor spending of $9.9 billion — which, if realized, would exceed the city's 2019 pre-pandemic record of $9.6 billion. In 2025, San Francisco welcomed 23.7 million visitors who spent $9.4 billion and supported 63,900 jobs in hotels, restaurants, retail, and cultural institutions.

The Downtown SF Partnership is also expanding its footprint significantly. The nonprofit community benefit district, which has covered 43 blocks in the Financial District and Jackson Square since 2019, is renewing its community benefit district charter 10 years ahead of schedule and expanding its coverage area to 70 blocks — nearly doubling its annual budget from roughly $6.3 million to more than $11 million. The expansion extends the district's reach to the waterfront, including Embarcadero Plaza.

Data published by the Partnership also shows a structural shift in how people engage with downtown: visitors are arriving for planned leisure and cultural outings, not just weekday work commutes. The Partnership's events calendar now draws more page views on Saturdays than any other day of the week, averaging 49.64% more Saturday traffic than Friday.

topStories.headline: SFMOMA Opens New Jacob Hashimoto Installation This Week — and Announces Blockbuster Fashion Show
topStories.dek: The San Francisco Museum of Modern Art debuts a major new free-admission installation this Saturday and announces its first fashion exhibition in 40 years, a Dior-to-McQueen survey opening in 2027.
topStories.body:
The San Francisco Museum of Modern Art (SFMOMA), at 151 Third Street on the edge of Union Square, is opening a significant new work this week. Jacob Hashimoto: Giant Arc, a monumental site-specific installation described as the artist's largest work to date, opens to the public Saturday, August 22, in the museum's admission-free Roberts Family Gallery on the first floor. The opening was previewed with a special Thursday Night talk and live performance on August 20.

SFMOMA also made a major programming announcement this week: the museum announced Fashioning Form: Dior to McQueen, its first major fashion exhibition in 40 years. The show, on view from April 17 through August 7, 2027, will present visionary fashion designs from the past eight decades in dialogue with postwar and contemporary sculpture. Tickets to the upcoming RM x SFMOMA exhibition, which brings together 200 works from BTS member RM's personal art collection and SFMOMA's holdings in a show opening in October, went on sale to the general public on August 11.

The museum remains open Tuesday through Sunday, with extended Thursday-evening hours until 8 p.m. Current on-view exhibitions include Graciela Iturbide: Between Two Worlds, Matisse's Femme au chapeau: A Modern Scandal, and the reinstalled Reimagined: The Fisher Collection at 10.

topStories.headline: Lids Returns to Union Square With Larger Store, Signaling Renewed Retail Confidence
topStories.dek: The sports hat retailer Lids is opening a new 2,100-square-foot location at 50 Powell St., three times the size of the store it closed in 2023 during the retail exodus from Union Square.
topStories.body:
Lids, the national sportswear retailer specializing in hats and licensed sports merchandise, has filed building permits for a new location at 50 Powell Street in Union Square, according to a report published August 11 by the San Francisco Standard. The company plans to open the store in November 2026.

The new location will be 2,100 square feet — three times the size of the former Lids store at 167 Powell Street that closed in 2023, when retailers were departing Union Square in significant numbers. The return is being read by downtown boosters as a signal of renewed confidence in the corridor. The Powell Street strip that runs along the cable car route has been visibly pocked with vacancies in recent years, a sore point for city leaders trying to rebuild downtown's reputation.

Lids joins other recent Union Square retail arrivals, including Nintendo's San Francisco flagship store, and Zara's announced plans for a new flagship. The new Powell Street location would place Lids near the heart of Union Square's retail district, within walking distance of Union Square Plaza and the Powell Street transit hub.

moreNews.headline: Financial District Weekday Workforce Climbs 18% as Return-to-Office Gains Momentum
moreNews.body: New cell phone mobility data published by The Registry SF on August 6 shows weekday worker activity across San Francisco's Financial District has climbed 18% compared to the prior year, as return-to-office mandates from both private employers and the city take hold. Mayor Daniel Lurie's directive requiring approximately 8,000 additional city workers to report in-person four days a week took effect earlier this year. The Downtown SF Partnership's Q2 2026 market report meanwhile shows falling office vacancy across all building classes in the district, and hotel RevPAR up 15.8% — additional indicators that foot traffic is translating into economic activity.

moreNews.headline: Downtown SF Partnership Expands to 70 Blocks, Nearly Doubling Its Budget
moreNews.body: The Downtown San Francisco Partnership is renewing and expanding its Community Benefit District — 10 years ahead of schedule — stretching its coverage from 43 to 70 city blocks and nearly doubling its annual budget from roughly $6.3 million to more than $11 million, according to a report in the San Francisco Chronicle. The expansion brings Embarcadero Plaza and waterfront spaces formally under the district's umbrella of cleaning, safety, and placemaking services. The Partnership's expanded mandate includes added street ambassador patrols, power washing, business recruitment, and activation of the Front Street Entertainment Zone.

moreNews.headline: SFMOMA Tickets for RM x SFMOMA Now on Sale to the Public
moreNews.body: Tickets for RM x SFMOMA: Between You and Me — a major exhibition co-curated by Kim Namjoon (RM of BTS) that brings together 200 works of Korean art and international contemporary art from RM's personal collection and SFMOMA's holdings — went on public sale on August 11. The show opens October 3, 2026, and runs through February 7, 2027. Member previews are scheduled for October 1–3.
